finding.title: hastub Store decodes with stdlib json: 6 of 6 hostile number tokens load where HA's orjson Store drops the file

finding.title: FlowCurveBias.observe raise aborts the cycle's accuracy pipeline and fails the whole update
finding.claim:
If FlowCurveBias.samples ever goes negative (the state flow_lift.py:210's `samples < 0` guard exists to refuse), coordinator._fold_flow_lift's call to FlowCurveBias.observe raises ZeroDivisionError uncaught, aborting HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._record_accuracy() before the accuracy-scoring calls that follow it in the same method, and propagating out of _async_update_data into its generic `except Exception` handler, which converts it to UpdateFailed for the whole cycle.

observe()'s low-sample branch divides by `self.samples + 1`; at samples=-1 that denominator is 0. _record_accuracy calls _fold_flow_lift (and therefore observe) before its own lead-time and DHW accuracy scoring, with no try/except around any of these per-cycle folds; _async_update_data's caller wraps only _command_frequency and _async_drive_pumps individually in try/except Exception ("never allowed to break the cycle"), but calls self._record_accuracy() with no such wrapper, so a raise there is caught only by the outer method's blanket except, which converts ANY exception into UpdateFailed -- the whole update, not just the fold, fails.

finding.title: A report-on-change indoor thermometer silent over 60 min turns Indoor Temperature unavailable
finding.claim: With the indoor thermometer's state '21.3' valid in Home Assistant but last reported 61, 90, 240 or 480 min ago, the integration's Indoor Temperature sensor is unavailable in 4 of 7 silence cells (available at 5-59 min), and a thermometer that re-writes an unchanged value (last_reported 5 min, last_updated 480 min) stays available, so the gaps come from genuine report silence, not from ignoring last_reported. Full original title (moved here by intake normalisation, 126 chars, over the 120-char schema limit): "A report-on-change indoor thermometer silent over 60 min turns Indoor Temperature unavailable while HA holds its valid reading"
finding.mechanism: InputReader._age_gate marks the indoor reading stale once its last_reported/last_updated age exceeds INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[indoor] = 60 min (x staleness scale, default 1.0); reading_ok['upper_floor_temperature'] goes False and _MeasuredTemperatureMixin.available follows it. A thermometer that reports only on change (common for battery Zigbee/BLE sensors: a stable room for hours sends nothing and Home Assistant writes nothing) therefore reads as dead, contradicting const.py's stated intent that the limits are 'generous multiples of a normal reporting interval so that a healthy sensor never trips them'. The user sees history gaps (reported: ~16:30-20:45 and ~03:30-06:15 local, the stable hours); the same stale flag also withholds the reading from the cycle. D1-s5-01's age_of seam (inlet/humidity) ignores last_reported, but this path does not: its re-report arm is available.

Too-eager question (orchestrator addendum): the guard is too eager exactly for report-on-change thermometers silent over 60 min (4 of 7 cells, every silence >= 61 min); an unchanged value that moves only last_reported does NOT trip it (rereport_unavailable=0 of 1). finding.title: Euler sub-step guard judges each store's diagonal ratio only, so coupled stores in accepted configs diverge
finding.claim: For configurations the config flow accepts, ThermalModel._stability_substeps leaves the per-substep Euler map with spectral radius > 1, and a zero-input 24 h trajectory diverges (69/3936 grid configs leave the passive envelope, 50 past 100 K; named point reaches -2.84e35 degC).
finding.mechanism: _stability_substeps bounds each store's (sum of couplings)/C*h by EULER_STABILITY_MAX_RATIO=1.5, on the premise that Euler is stable up to 2 per store. For coupled RC stores the stiff eigenvalue reaches the sum of the diagonal terms (Gershgorin: |lambda| <= 2*max diag), so lambda*h reaches 3 and the update oscillates with growth. Example: house mass 0.5, loss 0.2, slab mass 0.5, slab transfer 5.0 -> n_sub=2, radius 1.525.

finding.title: DHW refill coil debits the wood tank the full coil heat but spares the DHW tank only its scaled share
finding.claim: In simulate_trajectory_with_dhw with the wood coil active, for a DHW tank below DHW_MIXED_USE_TEMP, the wood tank loses more heat than the coil spares the DHW tank (non-zero in 28/28 cells, up to 0.406 kWh per 15-min step; 0.054 kWh at DHW 35 degC / wood 70 degC).
finding.mechanism: dhw_coil_draw_reduction splits the nominal draw into reduced+coil==draw and the wood tank is debited coil. simulate_dhw_step then scales the reduced draw by min(1,(T-inlet)/(40-inlet)), so the DHW tank is spared only scale*coil. (1-scale)*coil vanishes per step. The tap water is the same with or without the coil, because the coil only preheats the refill.

finding.title: Settlement caps (slab_settlement_cap, hold_demand_kw) ignore the learned house_heat_loss_scale the dynamics apply
finding.claim: optimizer.slab_settlement_cap and optimizer.hold_demand_kw size the steady-state demand from the raw zone losses. simulate_step multiplies those losses by house_heat_loss_scale (via effective_heat_loss_coefficient), and the sibling _buffer_charge_ceiling does the same. So at any learned scale other than 1, the 'sustaining' slab cap does not sustain the target: the room drifts at up to 1.44 K/h, the cap sits up to 13.5 K low (67.5 kWh of slab heat the terminal cost cannot see), and published predicted_savings are overstated by up to 13.4 currency at scale 2.
finding.mechanism: slab_settlement_cap: q_demand = u*(target-out) - gains, with u = heat_loss_coefficient or lower_floor_heat_loss_learned and no house_heat_loss_scale. hold_demand_kw has the same omission. Both feed _settlement_caps, which feeds _terminal_cost (the objective) and _deferred_energy_cost (the published savings). The dynamics and _buffer_charge_ceiling (the latter explicitly: 'a learned-leaky house that omitted it here got an optimistic ceiling') apply the scale.

finding.title: #1067 flow-lift bias clamp (15 K) cannot reach real supply: model curve tops out at 27.9 C, COP overstated up to 37%
finding.claim: With flow_curve_cop enabled, ThermalModel.compute_cop prices the direct-plant lift at curve_flow_temp + flow_curve_bias. The model's own curve never exceeds 27.9 C on the default houses, because emitter UA is derived from pump nameplate at a fixed 15 K, while the bias is clamped at FLOW_BIAS_CLAMP_K = 15 K. So a plant running at 40/45/50 C pins the bias at the clamp in every cell, and the priced COP exceeds the COP at the real supply by up to 8.4% / 22.8% / 36.8%.
finding.mechanism: flow_lift.FLOW_BIAS_CLAMP_K is justified in its comment against a 35 C curve ('a fixed-setpoint plant running 45 C against a curve asking 35 C is 10 K out'). But curve_supply_temp -> flow_target_for_indoor -> mixing_valve.flow_setpoint uses emitter_ua = max_electrical_power*cop_nominal/emitter_design_delta_t (15 K, not configurable), which gives 22-28 C curves. Residuals of 17-27 K are real installation offsets against this curve, but the clamp truncates them.

The flag is off by default, so no golden fixture moves except direct_flow_carnot if it enables the curve.

finding.title: Two-zone comfort penalty halves each zone's floor price; shipped plans sit up to 0.46 K below min_temp
finding.claim: On the stock two-zone house (tests/golden.py:make, winter_cold) the shipped plan's upper zone falls below min_temp 17.0 by 2.467 degree-steps summed over 12 price x DHW cells (1.314 in two|dhw|winter_typical, coldest 16.54 C), while the same house single-zone breaches 0.147 and every flat-price cell 0.
finding.mechanism: _comfort_terms (and _comfort_terms_batch) average the two zones' penalties with 0.5 x (...), which also halves each zone's quadratic floor term and its _COMFORT_FLOOR_L1 linear term; the constant's own comment says 2.0 is the smallest L1 that removes residual floor violations, so each zone of a two-zone house gets half of it and the solver buys the breach back where prices reward it (two|dhw|winter_typical: holding the floor costs 70.52 vs 67.50 SEK).

finding.title: coordinator.py tzinfo guards (:8112, :8384) are dead under the gate's naive clock; unblinded they crash
finding.claim:
coordinator.py:8384's `if when.tzinfo is None and now.tzinfo is not None: when = when.replace(tzinfo=now.tzinfo)` (and, by identical shape, :8112's) is unreachable under the gate's default environment, because dt_util.now() there is naive (HASTUB_TZ unset) so `now.tzinfo is not None` is always false; deleting the guard is then byte-identical (0.0 vs 0.0) on a 3-event, one-config scenario. Only once the coordinator's own clock is made timezone-aware (HASTUB_TZ=Europe/Stockholm, which only tests/dst_checks.py's subprocess sets, for a different file) does the deleted guard diverge -- not silently, but with an uncaught TypeError comparing an offset-naive and an offset-aware datetime.

finding.title: L-BFGS-B asks the scalar objective for f(x) every iterate at ~19-26x a batched row: 9-19% of the solve
finding.claim: _multi_start_minimize hands scipy a scalar fun and a batched jac separately, so every iterate evaluates the scalar objective (1.0-1.6 ms, 18.6-25.9x one batched row) before the 96-row gradient batch; that scalar path is 0.087-0.192 of optimize() thread CPU, and serving f from an extra row 0 of the same batch (jac=True) drops it to 0.005-0.018 with every plan bitwise unchanged.
finding.mechanism: scipy's ScalarFunction calls fun(x) then jac(x); the memo (#288) only saves the jac's f0 re-evaluation, not the scalar evaluation itself, which runs simulate_trajectory as a Python loop of simulate_step with a dataclasses.replace per step. The batched kernel's cost is per-call overhead amortised over rows, so a 97th row costs ~0.04-0.08 ms where the scalar call costs 1.0-1.6 ms. A one-row batch per scalar call is dearer still (recorded negative arm --via-batch: share 0.15 -> 0.31).

finding.title: Hot water without a tank probe: every solve starts from the 55 C ThermalState default, never advanced
finding.claim: With hot water configured and dhw_temp_entity omitted (the config flow's default install), the coordinator hands the solver dhw_temperature = 55.0 C on every cycle. In a 24-cycle closed loop, 23 of 24 solves start more than 1 K away from the tank the integration's own model says it left, and the model-truth tank spends 6.25 h of the demand windows below dhw_min_temperature, against 0 h with the probe mapped.
finding.mechanism: coordinator._update_current_state writes _current_state.dhw_temperature only from an ok reading of CONF_DHW_TEMP_ENTITY (coordinator.py ~5431), and no other producer advances it. So _solve_snapshot deep-copies the ThermalState dataclass default of 55.0 into every solve, and the optimizer uses initial_state.dhw_temperature as the tank's initial temperature. The plan therefore always believes the tank was just charged, schedules little DHW, and the next cycle resets to 55 again. _dhw_probe_temperature already fences this constant away from the display and the learners, but the solver is not fenced. slab_temperature is the same seam when floor_return_temp_entity is omitted: it is seeded once to room+1 K and never advanced (1 distinct solver-initial value in 24 solves, against 23-24 with the probe).

finding.title: Eight production seams still do wall-clock datetime arithmetic across DST; the forecast grid lands 60 min off
finding.claim: On every 2025-2027 Europe/Stockholm transition day the real coordinator cycle executes datetime arithmetic at 9 distinct production sites whose result differs from the UTC truth (8 instances plus tariff._window_slot, a wall-clock label by definition), and the worst (_forecast_arrays' step_offset) puts step 0 of the price/weather grid 60 min away from the solve anchor on 42 of 48 cycles.
finding.mechanism: Home Assistant hands every datetime the process-wide ZoneInfo instance; CPython subtracts two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo object as naive wall clock, and datetime+timedelta on a zoned value is wall-clock addition. _forecast_arrays computes step_offset=(now-midnight) in wall minutes, then _utc_step_starts walks UTC from midnight by that many steps, so after the transition the grid is 1 h late (spring) or early (autumn) and the plan is priced against the wrong hour for ~21 h. tests/dst_checks.py freezes only 00:07 (offset 0) so it never runs this path.

finding.title: Mutation ratchet inventory cannot see 528 of 2313 production guard seams; a new guard of those shapes raises it by 0
finding.claim: tests/mutation_table.py:candidates() yields no site on 528 of the 2313 guard seams in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer (52 of 1346 early-exit ifs, 246 of 668 clamps, 230 of 299 threshold ternaries). A new undispositioned guard whose test spans two lines therefore raises unpinned_sites by 0 and ratchet_refusal does not refuse, against +1 and refusal for the same guard on one line.
finding.mechanism: Six single-line operators. GUARD_OFF fires only on an if whose test is on one line, whose line starts with 'if ' and ends with ':', and which has no else; that misses multi-line tests (46), elif (3), a trailing comment after the colon (2) and else branches (1). CLAMP_DROP fires only on a bare min/max with exactly 2 args on one line; that misses numpy/math clamps (179), multi-line calls (63) and 3+ args (4). No operator touches a conditional expression's test. At their pre-fix commits, two of the six ledger I1 instances whose defect is a guard line are of an invisible shape: R5 D3-04 #1312 (the ternary len(positives) >= 2, 076f4a35^) and R5 D3-08 #1316 (np.clip in curve_learning._step_down, 6438f8f6^).

finding.proposed_fix_scope: Barrier in tests/mutation_table.py:candidates(). GUARD_OFF on any ast.If, rewriting the test's source segment (multi-line and elif included) to False. CLAMP_DROP on np.clip/np.minimum/np.maximum/np.fmin/np.fmax/math.fmin/fmax and on multi-line min/max calls. A seventh TERN operator that replaces a conditional expression's test with True. Mutants become multi-line edits, which per-worker tree copies already allow. Standing cost is AST-only: inventory() takes 3.77 s CPU today and this detector 3.91 s (provisional). The widening adds 528 sites at base and head alike, so no PR is refused by the widening itself, and the nightly burn-in inherits 528 more candidates to drive.
